2607.03426.title: Amortising Bayesian Experimental Design for Sequential Information Gathering in LLMs
2607.03426.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong reasoning and world-knowledge capabilities, yet often struggle to gather information effectively across the multi-turn interactions required in sequential decision-making settings. We introduce Amortised Sequential Information Gathering (ASIG), a fine-tuning approach that amortises Bayesian Experimental Design (BED) into LLM policies via a multi-turn extension of Group Relative Policy Optimisation with an Expected Information Gain reward. Evaluated on the 20 Questions task, ASIG more than doubles the success rate of the 7B base model and reduces inference cost by over $25\times$ relative to BED-LLM, a competitive inference-time baseline. Applied to MediQ, a medical diagnosis benchmark unseen during training, ASIG improves information-seeking performance at the 7B scale, suggesting that the learned strategies can transfer out of distribution. Our findings show that amortising BED into LLM policies provides an effective and computationally efficient approach to sequential information gathering.
2607.03426.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）展現出強大的推理和世界知識能力，但在需要多輪互動的序列決策環境中，往往難以有效地收集信息。我們引入了攤銷序列信息收集（ASIG），這是一種通過期望信息增益獎勵的多輪擴展的群體相對政策優化，將貝葉斯實驗設計（BED）攤銷到LLM政策中的微調方法。在20個問題任務上的評估中，ASIG使7B基礎模型的成功率翻倍以上，並將相對於BED-LLM（競爭性推理時間基準）的推理成本降低了超過$25\times$。應用於MediQ，一個在訓練期間未見的醫療診斷基準，ASIG在7B規模上提高了信息尋求的表現，這表明所學策略可以轉移到分佈外。我們的研究結果顯示，將BED攤銷到LLM政策中提供了一種有效且計算上高效的序列信息收集方法。
